Este é o quadro que organiza tudo: seis: This is the chart that organises everything: six cases × three genders × singular and plural. Read it by columns: each column (masculine, feminine, neuter, plural) has its own pattern. The golden rule of the accusative: if the noun is inanimate (a thing), the accusative equals the nominative in the masculine, the neuter and the plural; in the feminine, -а becomes -у. If it is animate (a person or an animal), the accusative equals the genitive in the masculine and in the plural. The prepositional always comes with a preposition (в, на, о, при) and in the plural it ends in -ах or -ях. Examples: стол (m), книга (f), окно (n).

Os seis casos: adjetivos e possessivos: The six cases: adjectives and possessives
O adjetivo e o possessivo mudam junto co: The adjective and the possessive change along with the noun and always agree with it in gender, number and case. A trick: the adjective endings resemble the question of the case («какой? какого? какому? каким? о каком?»). The accusative follows the same rule as the nouns: inanimate = nominative; animate masculine and animate plural = genitive. Prepositional: -ом / -ой / -ом / -ых. English adjectives never change ("a new book", "with a new book"), so this agreement is new.
I am reading a new book.
I am going with my friend.
I live in a big city.
The adjective goes into the accusative too.
The possessive and the noun change together.

Pronomes e preposições com cada caso: Pronouns and prepositions with each case
Os pronomes pessoais mudam nos seis caso: Personal pronouns change in the six cases; after a preposition, the 3rd-person ones gain an н-: «у него», «к ней», «с ними». Each preposition takes a fixed case (or two, depending on the question): remember the rule of the questions «где?» (staying) and «куда?» (moving). For "in, on, at" with movement: accusative; staying put: prepositional. English shows the same case idea only in a few pronouns (I / me / my), so use that as a hook.
